en.title: Strictly Increasing Array After Removing One Subarray
en.description:
Given an array of positive integers, removing one non-empty contiguous subarray is a valid removal if the remaining array (which may be empty) is strictly increasing. Count all valid removals.

The standard input/output, the ranges added by this site, and the examples follow this problem's description; wherever the source's ranges are missing, they are explicitly marked as this site's additions.
en.input: The first line contains n (1≤n≤100000); the second line contains n positive integers, 1≤nums[i]≤10^9. The ranges are taken from the original problem's constraints.
en.output: Output the number of valid contiguous subarrays, stored as a 64-bit integer.
en.explanation: Find the longest strictly increasing prefix and suffix. Enumerate the kept prefix length i, and use two pointers to find the earliest suffix start j that joins it while keeping the array strictly increasing; every suffix start after j also works, so accumulate the number of ways.
